correctness.rationale: For the strictly positive ternary digit basis split into even and odd exponent positions, derived the base-nine B+3B decomposition with B-digits 0,1,2 and unique mixed split, including the required nonzero-summand conditions. Unordered same-part pair counts follow from the digit convolution (1,2,3,2,1), subtraction of two zero-summand ordered solutions, and reinsertion of the diagonal. The carry-automaton intersection is 2^(2k-1); inclusion–exclusion on mixed-support numbers and explicit pure-support exceptions contribute 3^k-3k and 3^k-2k-1, giving 8·5^(k-1)-2^(2k-1)-5k for every k>=1. Verified R(n)=0 only at n=0,1. An independently written exhaustive enumeration of every positive unordered pair and every n<9^k for k=1..5 agrees: nonunique counts (1,22,153,852,4463). No finite-k experiment is substituted for the all-k combinatorial argument.
residual_risks: Result limited to this parity partition and cutoffs 9^k, not arbitrary partitions or continuous cutoffs.
Carry-state uniform proof, not tests at k<=5, supports all k.
